experiment_name: Value-generalization probe: unbiased TEST-set read after fixing 020's validation-doubles-as-early-stopping and first-N sampling gaps

algorithm_config.opponents: none - all 4 seats are baseline_pretraining.pt, clean self-play, zero fixed agents, zero ASU
algorithm_config.split: 64 TRAIN / 16 SELECTION / 16 TEST games - TEST touched exactly once, only for the final 64-train-game model; never used for early stopping, hyperparameter/temperature selection, or model choice
algorithm_config.sampling_method: quantile-spread (min/median/max of available occurrences per game/seat/bucket) - fixes 020's first-N clustering
algorithm_config.label: actor-relative one-hot of the REAL final winner
algorithm_config.value_probe_architecture: same as 020: own-written MLP 300 -> Linear(256) -> ReLU -> Linear(4), CPU, reused directly from monopolyzero_value_learnability_probe.py
baselines_compared: probabilistic net-worth-leader (temperature-scaled softmax, temperature fit on TRAIN+SELECTION pooled only, never TEST)
algorithm_config.learning_curve_evaluated_on: SELECTION only, for all three points including the 64-game one (TEST is not touched repeatedly)
algorithm_config.uncertainty_method: game-block (not state-level) bootstrap - states from the same game are correlated, so the unit of resampling is the game

loss.note: SELECTION loss (0.814, the early-stopping criterion) vs. the truly-unseen TEST cross-entropy (1.182) for the identical final model - the gap between these two numbers is exactly what 020 could not measure, since its own validation split played both roles at once

result: Purely descriptive measurement, no GO/KILL threshold applied (per the task's own instruction). 96/96 games completed cleanly (0 illegal, 0 crashes, 0 fixed-agent fallbacks - no fixed agents were seated - 0 ASU modules loaded). All pairwise seed and state leakage guards across TRAIN/SELECTION/TEST read zero. Quantile-spread sampling visibly worked: TEST bucket round provenance spans each bucket's full range (e.g. 151-terminal: min 151, median 174.5, max 199), unlike 020's first-N clustering. On the untouched 16-game TEST set (759 states, evaluated exactly once with the final 64-train-game model): the probabilistic net-worth-leader baseline (temperature=500, fit on TRAIN+SELECTION only) is the strongest predictor on every metric (CE 0.063, Brier 0.032, accuracy 96.6%), the hard/epsilon-smoothed leader is close behind on accuracy (96.3%) but scores worse on CE (0.510) since it is penalized hard whenever wrong, and the learned ValueProbe (CE 1.182, Brier 0.643, accuracy 55.5%) barely beats uniform (CE 1.386, accuracy 30.0%) and is clearly worse than both leader baselines on every metric this time, including cross-entropy - unlike 020's validation-contaminated read, where the learned probe had actually beaten the leader baseline on cross-entropy. The game-block bootstrap (unit of resampling = TEST game, not state, since a game's ~8 sampled states are correlated) confirms this is not sampling noise: learned-minus-probabilistic-leader 95% CIs exclude zero in the adverse direction on all three metrics (cross-entropy +1.119 [+0.747, +1.555], Brier +0.612 [+0.450, +0.762], accuracy -0.411 [-0.503, -0.309], n=16 games). The SELECTION-based learning curve (16/32/64 train games: CE 1.105 -> 1.015 -> 0.814, accuracy 46.2% -> 52.3% -> 69.2%) still shows no plateau at 64 games, and the SELECTION accuracy at 64 games (69.2%) is close to 020's old validation figure (69.2%, coincidentally identical to 3 significant figures) while the true TEST accuracy for the same model is only 55.5% - a real generalization gap that 020's design could not have detected, since its validation split was also its stopping criterion. No claim is made about POLICY_ONLY/PUCT/MonopolyZeroNet strength; no win-rate evaluation or PUCT was run; the policy network's own weights were never touched.
notes: Full per-bucket breakdown, calibration bins, and confusion matrices for all four TEST predictors, plus the full temperature grid search (500.0 chosen, CE 0.0735 on TRAIN+SELECTION pooled - the next-best grid points were 200.0 at 0.0811 and 1000.0 at 0.1129, a fairly flat/broad minimum), are in the raw stdout log (28.8KB), not duplicated here. bucket_provenance in the raw log also covers TRAIN and SELECTION splits, not just TEST, all showing similarly full within-bucket round spread. State-level N (759 TEST states) must not be read as 759 independent samples - the state_level_n_warning field in the raw log flags this explicitly, and the game_block_bootstrap result (16 games) is the correct uncertainty quantification for the learned-vs-probabilistic-leader comparison.
